title: third-party scorer deserialization: match the allow-listed module exactly, never by package prefix
answers: Why does loading a registered RAGAS, DeepEval, TruLens or Phoenix scorer fail with "module ... is not in the allow-list" when the module path points under a run artifact?
I'm adding a new DeepEval or RAGAS scorer module. What must change so a stored scorer from it still deserializes?
Where is the allow-list for third-party scorer imports enforced when a scorer is loaded back?
Why does loading a third-party scorer reject a class that is not a Scorer subclass?
body:
Path: Restoring a saved third-party scorer from its stored third_party_scorer_data (module, class, metric_name, kwargs) passes through mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py:Scorer.model_validate, which gates importlib.import_module on mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py:THIRD_PARTY_SCORER_ALLOWED_MODULES.
Rule: Allow-list membership is exact string equality (`module_path not in THIRD_PARTY_SCORER_ALLOWED_MODULES`); never use startswith or package-prefix matching. A dotted descendant of an allowed package can be a file placed by a caller (for example a run artifact under a file:// experiment artifact root), and import_module would execute its top-level code before any class check. The set holds the 14 modules that define the supported scorer classes: the four package roots plus their `scorers` submodules. After import, the resolved attribute must pass inspect.isclass and issubclass(..., Scorer) before it is instantiated.
Symptom: A third-party scorer payload whose module was a descendant of an allowed package (e.g. mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens.<run_id>.artifacts.payload) was imported and executed on load, so a caller who could write under the server's artifact root could run code through scorer loading.
Constraints: Applies only to deserialization of third-party scorers. A new scorer-defining module must be added to THIRD_PARTY_SCORER_ALLOWED_MODULES explicitly; the completeness test test_third_party_scorer_allow_list_is_exactly_the_scorer_defining_modules AST-scans the four packages and fails if the set differs from the modules that define Scorer subclasses. Serializers emit the defining module, so stored payloads from earlier releases still load.
applies: Scorer deserialization for ragas, deepeval, trulens and phoenix third-party scorers in mlflow/genai/scorers; any change to how the module path of a stored scorer is resolved.
says: Loading a saved third-party evaluation scorer fails with an allow-list error.
Saved evaluation judges fail to load when pointing under experiment run artifacts.
Prevent arbitrary code execution vulnerabilities when restoring saved third-party evaluation scorers.
Support deserializing stored evaluation metrics when adding new third-party scorer modules.
search: Third-party scorer deserialization in mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py:Scorer.model_validate checks module_path against mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py:THIRD_PARTY_SCORER_ALLOWED_MODULES using exact string equality, never startswith or package-prefix matching. This prevents executing arbitrary code from caller-placed files under run artifact roots before class validation, requiring imported attributes to pass inspect.isclass and issubclass(..., Scorer). Applies only to deserializing ragas, deepeval, trulens, and phoenix scorers; new scorer-defining modules must be explicitly added to THIRD_PARTY_SCORER_ALLOWED_MODULES, as tested by test_third_party_scorer_allow_list_is_exactly_the_scorer_defining_modules.
